sampling_model.design: Deterministic selection of proxy-intervention distributions indexed by \(A\); the design randomness and finite-sample allocation are outside this combinatorial identification scope.
sampling_model.units: Vertices of a fixed finite semi-Markovian causal graph \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: Acquisition of the interventional laws associated with the selected proxy variables in \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity required by the imported generalized-identification semantics is held fixed and is not strengthened by the optimization results.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the target is experiment acquisition sufficient for graphical identification, not estimation from finite samples.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix D.2 gives polynomial optimization when every minimal hedge residual has size at most two, while fixed larger size only makes enumeration polynomial and leaves hitting set exponential.
Theorems 1--2 encode MCID feasibility as SAT and then WPMAX-SAT or ILP, and the conclusion leaves efficient approximation as future work.
Theorem 6 and Corollaries 2--3 make hedges complete graphical witnesses for failure of interventional identification.
Optimal fractional vertex-packing solutions have half-integral basic optima and their integral coordinates persist in an integral optimum.
Theorem 3.1 establishes APX-completeness of minimum vertex cover on cubic graphs.
Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, minimum vertex cover has no polynomial approximation factor below two.
The vertex-cover LP integrality gap on a graph is \(2-2/\chi^f(G)\).
Weighted \(d\)-Hitting Set with an explicit hyperedge list admits parameterized search-tree algorithms.

body.tldr: Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for bow-free singleton-target ADMGs. Four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes the edge clutter of every ordered simple graph exactly, yielding unit-cost NP and APX hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. The same path classification partitions every rank-three residual across target parents and spouses, which gives a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm; complete-graph expansions attain gap \(2-2/n\), and the Khot--Regev threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\). Promised enumeration and an optimizer-or-rank-violation interface connect the theorem to existing exact solvers, while unrestricted rank-three recognition remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: The published MCID frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness. It does not identify the first nonempty bow-free singleton rank or its causal-specific approximation ratio.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition, yet the class is expressive enough to realize every graph edge clutter through private guards.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact four-vertex obstruction classification and representation theorem, transfers objective-preserving hardness, derives a tight factor-two LP frontier, and gives a certifying interface that is useful without asserting an unrestricted rank recognizer.

body.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the complete hedge obstruction used to interpret residual hitting as causal identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash formulate MCID as minimum-weight hedge hitting, prove unrestricted hardness, and settle bounded residual size through two; their Appendix D.2 is the direct boundary this paper continues. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow the immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the rounding argument, although the proposed parent-spouse threshold proof is stated directly on causal residuals. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover APX hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred by the exact private-guard realization. Singh's LP-gap formula motivates the complete-graph family but is not claimed to be sharpened. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The private-guard reverse inclusion and the parent-spouse rounding are universal informal arguments that require independent proof checking. The solver interface does not recognize \(r(G,s)\leq3\) from a successful run. Weighted \(O(3^k)\) exact search is claimed only with a supplied cardinality bound, not as an unconstrained optimizer parameterized by an unknown optimum cardinality.
body.honest_scope: The central classification, exact realization, hardness transfer, rounding bound, and gap family are theorem targets. General positivity-based equivalence between hedge hitting and interventional identification, source complexity theorems, and rational LP solution are imported. The complexity of recognizing rank at most three, planar bounded-degree causal realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open. The reduction to a one-edge source graph recovers the unique four-vertex hedge, while \(r(G,s)\leq2\) reduces to the empty-intervention result, providing the required standard sanity checks.
